connections.why: Velocity and acceleration are defined as derivatives of position; without the limit-based derivative, instantaneous velocity is only a slogan, and constant-acceleration formulas cannot be derived rather than memorized.
Work is the accumulation of force over displacement; treating it as an integral explains why variable forces such as springs and gravity at large distances yield energy formulas.
The characteristic-equation roots determine whether motion oscillates, decays or overshoots; damping regimes and resonance are results of that algebra, not separate facts.
Expanding any potential about a minimum yields a quadratic term first, which is why harmonic motion is universal for small displacements and why the pendulum approximation sinθ≈θ works.
Divergence and curl are the differential form of flux and circulation; Maxwell's equations and the wave equation for light cannot be stated, let alone derived, without them.
Observables are Hermitian operators whose eigenvalues are measurement outcomes; the structure of quantum mechanics is spectral theory on complex vector spaces.
Representing x(t) as Re[Ae^{iωt}] converts differentiation into multiplication and phase addition into complex multiplication, simplifying driven oscillators and later wave and quantum amplitudes.
A capacitor that discharges through a resistor satisfies dV/dt = −V/RC, so the same first-order ODE explains cooling, drug clearance and passive membrane charging.
A lipid bilayer insulates (capacitance) while channels leak (resistance); the membrane time constant τ=RC sets how fast neurons integrate input, so circuit analysis becomes neurophysiology.
Equilibrium requires equal electrochemical potential; the Boltzmann factor gives the ratio of ion concentrations that balances an electric potential, which is exactly the Nernst equation.
A channel's open probability depends on the energy difference between open and closed states; Boltzmann statistics produce the sigmoidal voltage dependence used in gating models.

Neurotransmitter must diffuse across the cleft within about a millisecond; diffusion time scaling (t∝L²/D) shows why the cleft is tens of nanometres wide and why synaptic speed is physically constrained.
The HH equations have no closed-form solution; understanding step size, stability and error order determines whether a simulated spike is trustworthy.
Whether a neuron fires at arbitrarily low rate or has a minimum rate corresponds to different bifurcations (saddle-node vs Hopf); phase-plane language turns behavioural differences into geometry.
Spike counts are noisy; Poisson-like statistics define how much information a population carries and how well a stimulus can be decoded.
Power, effect size and error control determine how many measurements an experiment needs and what its result can license; design and analysis must be planned together.
In a linear recurrent network, connectivity eigenvalues decide whether activity decays, persists or explodes; this makes working-memory persistence a spectral statement.
Backpropagation is the chain rule applied efficiently over a computational graph, so understanding it exposes both its power and its biological implausibility.
STDP and LTP/LTD data constrain mathematical learning rules; analysing those rules shows what computations (e.g., PCA extraction) local plasticity can perform.
Both are inverse-square central forces, so Kepler-type orbit methods and Gauss's law reasoning transfer; the sign difference (attraction only vs both signs) explains neutrality and screening.
Minimizing travel time over the refraction point yields Snell's law, showing a physical law as an optimization result and foreshadowing variational principles.
Michaelis–Menten kinetics is a nonlinear first-order ODE that saturates unlike pure exponential decay; comparing the two clarifies what linear models miss in biochemical systems.
Random-walk simulations let one verify MSD∝t and explore geometries where the diffusion equation cannot be solved analytically.
Simulation yields results only if replicates, seeds and parameter ranges are chosen deliberately; Monte Carlo error scaling informs how many runs are needed.
Order-of-magnitude reasoning and units checks reveal which terms in a model matter and catch errors before any simulation is run.

A channel switching between conformations with fixed rates is a continuous-time Markov chain; the master equation gives macroscopic relaxation, and the stochastic version explains channel noise at small numbers.
Mutual information turns the question of what a response says about a stimulus into a number, and the data-processing inequality limits what downstream circuits can recover.
The passive cable equation is the diffusion equation with a leak term, so separation of variables and mode decay explain voltage spread and temporal smearing along dendrites.
Maintaining ion gradients costs ATP through pumps; the energetic cost of signaling is a physical constraint on neural coding and circuit size.
Poiseuille's r^4 law explains how small changes in vessel radius control blood flow, so regulation by vasodilation is physically very effective.
Radioactive decay is the simplest Markov jump process; the same exponential waiting times and Poisson counts appear in channel gating and spike generation.
Whether a Fourier series converges, and in what sense, requires pointwise versus uniform convergence; this explains Gibbs overshoot instead of treating it as an oddity.
The Boltzmann distribution is the maximum-entropy distribution at fixed mean energy, so statistical mechanics can be read as inference under constraints.
